metadata.title: Analytical soliton solutions of the ill-posed Boussinesq equation via a unified approach

references.text: method. Optik, 130, 1312-1319. Analytical soliton solutions are analyzed utilizing robust integration techniques (unified) which is new and distinct from results obtained by using other approaches. The following observations are provided by using the suitable values for the unknown coefficients and regular measurements to describe the visual result of these solutions with three dimensional and two dimensional density graphs. The 3D and density plots are used to explore physical phenomena of our observations, the observations are as follows: Fig. (1) and Fig. (2) depict the periodic waves of the Eq. (3.7) and Eq. (3.8) solutions. Fig. (3,5,8) and Fig. (9) depict the dark solitons of the Eq. (3.10), (3.15), (3.19) and Eq. (3.22) solutions. The kink shaped wave profile for the solution of Eq. (3.14) is shown in Fig. (4). The anti-Kink shaped soliton of solution of Eq. (3.18) is displayed in Fig. (7). A dispersion-less soliton of solution of Eq. (3.16) is shown in Fig. (6). As a result, we used Maple software to analyze the answers we found by converting them back to the original Boussinesq equation using mathematical symbols. This paper proposes a Unified approach technique to solve the ill-possed Boussinesq equation and produces different new solutions and the solutions we obtained from the unified approach method has not been published yet. Also, these new solutions may provide us with the current findings and aid in providing much greater clarity for the equations physical characteristics. Using Maple software, the solutions are obtained. This method is very general as well as simple and easy for finding the exact solutions of non-linear partial differential equations which shows the efficiency, productivity and suitability of this method for handling many other non-linear partial differential equations (NPDE’s)
